notes: Summary: Ironbark is an enterprise financial software provider evaluating Redwood Dedicated / Private for production inference of trading and portfolio tools. Biggest priorities are predictable throughput during market hours, strict latency SLOs, and legalized SLA credit mechanics.

Workload specifics: sustained 150-200 QPS at peak business windows; burst up to 400 QPS for market open; P50 latency target <= 50ms for small chat/rerank calls, P95 <= 250ms. For certain trading-critical endpoints they require 'fast-path' routing with P99 < 500ms SLA.

Reserved GPU planning: initial ask is 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) dedicated, with headroom to burst 2x for market opens. They want a clear plan showing how Redwood maps GPU types to equivalent throughput and a timeline for adding capacity (within 48h for dedicated pools).

SLA & uptime: Ironbark legal is pushing for 99.95% monthly uptime for production endpoints. They want a graduated credit schedule and explicit maximum total downtime over rolling 12 months. Redwood suggested 99.9% for standard dedicated and 99.95% for an enhanced SLA with pricing uplift.
- Ironbark proposal: pro rata credits starting at >0.01% downtime, escalating to 100% credits for outages >12 hours in a month; termination right after 3 incidents >2 hours within 180 days.

- Redwood counter: tiered credits: 5% monthly usage credit for 99.9-99.95, 15% for 99.5-99.9, 50% for <99.5; limit per-incident cap; no single-incident termination but right to exit after repeated SLA breaches with cure periods.

Maintenance windows: Ironbark insists maintenance must not overlap core US market hours (13:30-21:00 UTC). They requested a monthly 2-hour maintenance window outside these hours only, with 48h notice and ability to opt-out for critical windows.

Support response times requested: Sev1 (production down impacting trading) — 15 minute phone/Slack response, 1 hour follow-up; Sev2 — 1 hour response; Sev3 — 4 hour response. Redwood proposed SLO-aligned SLAs with 24/7 on-call and dedicated escalation path for Sev1.

Security/compliance asks: on-prem KMS/HSM support for private deployment (must be FIPS-compliant), 7-year audit log retention option, SOC2 + ISO baseline, and data residency in US-only regions for trading data.

POC plan: 3-day dedicated POC (load + latency tests) followed by 2-week pilot in canary mode. Acceptance criteria: sustained throughput at target QPS with P95 latency <= 250ms and no data leakage in KMS integration. POC target dates proposed: Apr 6-8 (POC), Apr 13-27 (pilot).

Commercial hooks: CFO expects committed monthly spend with discounts for 12- and 24-month reserved capacity. CFO requests clear 'cost per token' and 'cost per QPS' for both dedicated and private modes.
Quotes from calls: 'We need contractual certainty around capacity and meaningful credits if you miss that — trading windows don't forgive downtime.' — Head of SRE (Ironbark).

Next legal items: provide a clean SLA table (uptime thresholds, per-incident credit caps, aggregate caps), a sample maintenance notice template, and a statement of remedy timeline. We promised to produce a redlined SLA doc by 2026-03-15.
